sections.h2: What a Rochester Hills sale involves
sections.html:
Rochester Hills is a high-value Oakland County suburb, yet the paperwork is modest: a deed filed with the county, two affidavits for the city's Assessing Department, and a treasurer's tax certificate. Most of the work happens at the county and state level.

Downtown Detroit is roughly 25 miles south. A 1984 charter vote turned Avon Township into the City of Rochester Hills. The older city of Rochester incorporated in 1967 and remains a separate municipality, a distinction buyers often blur, so make sure a listing or deed names the right one. When the title company asks for a legal description, match it to the parcel number on your tax bill.

The July 2025 estimate of 77,539 residents sits 1.6 percent above the 76,321 counted at the 2020 base, across 32.80 square miles of land.

Roughly three homes in four are lived in by their owners, which leaves little rental stock competing with your listing.

Rochester Community Schools serve most of the city, with Rochester Adams High School, Rochester High School and Stoney Creek High School all inside the city limits. Part of Rochester Hills falls in the Avondale School District instead, where many addresses are zoned to Deer Field Elementary in the city, while others go to Auburn Elementary in Auburn Hills or Woodland Elementary in Troy.

All Avondale residents attend Avondale Middle School in Rochester Hills and Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. Addresses in different parts of the city can belong to different districts, so get an official boundary check before a listing names a school.

The city keeps no police department of its own, and the Oakland County Sheriff's Office provides police service. The 52nd District Court's third division sits in the city. The city runs the Rochester Hills Public Library and, by contract, lets residents of the city of Rochester and Oakland Township use it. When a buyer asks about services, send them to the city's website and the sheriff's office.

Two documents go to the Assessing Department at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive: a Property Transfer Affidavit and, for an owner-occupant, a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit. The city expects the closing agent to give the buyer both, and they can be mailed or dropped off during weekday office hours.

The exemption lifts up to 18 mills of school tax off a bill when the owner lives there as a main residence. Sellers should ask Assessing for the rescission form so the exemption on the old home ends cleanly. The department also handles exemption requests based on income, and those have to be refiled every year.

A buyer who wants a quick tax estimate can halve the estimated value and apply the current millage rate, or ask Assessing to run it. An owner who disputes a value gets one chance a year: the March Board of Review, after the February notice.

sections.h2: Filing the deed in Oakland County
sections.html:
A deed filed with the Oakland County Register of Deeds costs $30, which already contains the state's $4 survey surcharge. A discharge or assignment that cites several earlier recordings adds $3 for each extra reference, and copies run $1 a page.

The county treasurer must certify warranty deeds and land contracts first, for $5. When you mail the deed, the Register of Deeds can obtain that certificate if your payment includes the extra $5. Expect about two weeks to get a hand-delivered document back and two to four weeks by mail.

Transfer tax runs $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. A deed with consideration under $100 is exempt, and any other claimed exemption must appear on the deed. The seller carries the bill under MCL 207.523.

sections.h2: Tax due dates around your closing
sections.html:
The summer bill covers school and county levies only. It is payable July 1 through September 14, and 1 percent interest starts September 15. Winter bills open December 1 and fall due in mid-February.

  • The city shows February 16, 2027 as the winter due date for the 2026 tax year, with a 3 percent penalty shortly after.
  • Anything still owed turns delinquent on March 2 and moves to the Oakland County Treasurer.
  • Postmarks do not count, so pay in person or online close to a deadline.
  • E-check payments are free online, while cards and mobile wallets add a 2.75 percent processing charge.

The winter bill adds the city's own levy for police and fire services, roads and the library, so a fall or winter closing can land before it is paid. Have the title company say who pays it and how it is credited, and use the Treasury tax look-up to see each parcel's status.

sections.h2: Preparing before you sign a contract
sections.html: Look up your parcel in the Treasury tax look-up and note anything unpaid. Ask Assessing for the rescission form, and ask the Building Department whether any inspection applies to your address before you choose a closing date. Decide whether you will mail the deed or have the closing agent carry it in, since mailing adds time. Send the buyer's closing agent the legal description that matches your tax bill, so the county examines a clean document the first time.

sections.h2: A cash sale and the same paperwork
sections.html:
Selling for cash does not change the filings. The deed still goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds, the treasurer still certifies a warranty deed, and the two Assessing affidavits still follow the closing. What a cash buyer removes is the lender: no appraisal gap, no loan approval deadline and no repair list demanded by a bank.

That can matter in a city where most houses are owner-occupied and buyers expect a clean, documented sale. Ask each buyer for the closing date they can commit to, then check it against the tax calendar above and the two to four weeks that a mailed deed can take to come back.

sections.h2: Questions buyers ask about the house
sections.html: Expect questions about the school district, the tax bill and any work you did. Keep your Principal Residence Exemption records handy so you can explain why the buyer's tax picture will differ from yours. Bring permit sign-offs for any addition, finished basement or new mechanical work. If a buyer asks about services, point to the city's website and the Oakland County Sheriff's Office rather than guessing.

faqs.q: Where is a Rochester Hills deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Register of Deeds, for $30 including the $4 survey surcharge. Warranty deeds first need a $5 treasurer certificate.

faqs.q: Must a Rochester Hills house pass a city inspection before closing?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Building Department whether one applies to your address, and do it before you pick a closing date. The Assessing Department only handles tax forms.

faqs.q: What paperwork does a Rochester Hills buyer owe the city?
faqs.a: A Property Transfer Affidavit, and an exemption affidavit for a buyer who will live there. Both go to Assessing at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive.

faqs.q: What are the tax deadlines in Rochester Hills?
faqs.a: September 14 for summer and mid-February for winter, shown as February 16, 2027 for the 2026 bill. Oakland County takes over unpaid balances on March 2.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax on a Rochester Hills sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The county charges $3.75 per $500 for the state portion and $0.55 per $500 for its own.
